original_question: Does every metric on a compact surface of positive genus have a geodesic that is dense in the surface?
target_in_paper: Question 8.4.2 in Section 8.4 ("Density in the manifold"): "Does every metric on a compact surface of positive genus have a geodesic that is dense in the surface?"
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's official formulation almost verbatim. It correctly identifies the exact open problem in the paper, keeps the scope on compact surfaces of positive genus, and asks for the existence of a single geodesic whose image is dense in the whole surface. It also stays narrower than the neighboring Question 8.4.1 about whether the union of all closed geodesics is dense.
missing_details: In the nearby context, the relevant ambient class is smooth Riemannian metrics; the paper uses separate language when it means Finsler metrics or magnetic structures.
The paper's standing convention is that the manifold is connected and smooth, so the surface should be understood as a compact connected smooth surface.
The quantifiers should be made explicit: for every such surface and every such metric, there exists at least one geodesic with the stated property.

The phrase "a geodesic that is dense in the surface" should be unpacked as a geodesic gamma: R -> S whose image has closure equal to S; in the paper geodesics are denoted gamma_v and are parametrized by arclength.
Section 8.4 explicitly frames this as an every-metric question, not a generic-metrics question.
refined_question: For every compact connected smooth surface S with genus(S) >= 1 and every smooth Riemannian metric g on S, must there exist a geodesic gamma: R -> S whose image is dense in S, i.e. such that the closure of gamma(R) is all of S?
justification: The draft is already essentially the exact wording of Question 8.4.2, so the correct refinement is only to make explicit the paper's standing conventions and nearby context, not to broaden it to the neighboring Question 8.4.1 or to a genericity/transitivity question. Section 1 supplies the conventions that M is a connected smooth manifold and that geodesics are the arclength-parametrized curves gamma_v. Section 8.4 says these are questions about density in M itself and explicitly says the metrics are not assumed generic. The surrounding Section 8.3 fixes the metric space under discussion as smooth Riemannian metrics.
